Active catheters and guide wires move like a snake using distributed NiTi shape memory alloy (SMA) coil actuators.
The active catheter can bend, torsion (twist), and extend by changing SMA actuator configurations.
Communication and control IC chips embedded in the catheter reduce the number of lead wires to three common wires.
An active guide wire of 0.5 mm diameter was developed using a flat meandering SMA actuator.
The active guide wire can bend over 60 degrees with a 5 mm bending length by applying 50 mA current at 25°C.
The outer tube of the active catheter is made of evaporated parylene and biocompatible polyurethane.
A micromachined fiber-optic pressure sensor with 125 µm diameter was developed for catheter use.
The fiber-optic pressure sensor is electrically safe and immune to electromagnetic interference.
A forward-looking ring array ultrasonic probe with piezoelectric PZT ceramic transducers is mounted at the catheter tip.
The ultrasonic probe enables real-time 3D imaging of blood vessels without saline flushing.
Three-axis magneto-impedance sensors detect Earth's magnetic field and AC magnetic fields for catheter tip localization.
Batch assembly methods using nickel electroplating and acrylic electrodeposition enable low-cost fabrication.
The active catheter achieved a 60-degree bending angle at 32 mm length with 80 mA current at 25°C in air.
Surface temperature of the catheter during actuation was kept below 41°C in water at 38°C with 80 mA current.
Integrated circuits and sensors near the catheter tip help reduce X-ray exposure during interventions.
The active catheter's multi-joint mechanism is controlled remotely from outside the body.
The active catheter's diameter is approximately 1.4 mm.
The active guide wire consists of a meandering SMA actuator and a coil spring for flexibility.
The magnetic sensor system allows 3D navigation by superimposing catheter position on vessel maps from CT or MR angiography.
Future multifunctional active catheters may provide virtual reality-like feedback to doctors.
